A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PSA research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison. The appendices match apart from page numbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original alignment, text-generation, MMLU, model-scaling, membership-inference, and ablation results in Sections 5–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the privacy-attack experiments and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same difference-vector computation, clipping, normalization, Gaussian noise, and inference-time activation addition. The canary-based membership-inference procedure in Algorithm 3 is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same seven alignment behaviors, their open-ended questions, MMLU, and hallucination-based canary attacks. The appendix retains the same negative-steering scenarios.

E2.justification: PCA Steering/In-Context Vectors, Mean Steering, and zero-shot evaluation retain their membership in the corresponding comparisons. Table 7 still compares Mean Steering with PSA for both attacked models.

E3.justification: The model configurations, Qwen size sweep, dataset sample counts, steering settings, evaluation metrics, and GPT-4 judging procedures are unchanged. The attack still uses 100 outputs at temperature 0.8 with the same model-specific thresholds.

E4.justification: Appendix D retains the noise and clipping sensitivity studies, zero-noise clipping control, and negative-steering analyses. The model-scaling analysis and qualitative examples also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same 1000-trial membership-inference evaluation and empirical privacy estimation procedure. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-reporting information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results, plots, and qualitative outputs are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. The transposed tables preserve their values; for example, PSA's hallucination GPT-4 score remains 3.94 in Table 3 and its corresponding MMLU score remains 63.2 in Table 5.

T1.justification: The DP definition, Facts 2.1–2.3, steering equations, and composition/post-processing argument are unchanged. Section 3 replaces zi with the already-defined demonstration tuple, clarifying notation without changing the protected record or assumptions.

C1.justification: The novelty, privacy, utility, and membership-inference contributions retain their scope. Although the abstract removes a sentence specifying that the attack needs only generated text, Section 6 retains that claim explicitly.

C2.justification: The explanations of noise effects, model-size scaling, and clipping/normalization tradeoffs are unchanged. Appendix E retains the same limitations concerning mean steering, restricted alignment axes, and monolingual evaluation.

D1.justification: Both versions provide the same code-access information, model chat-template details, evaluation prompts, canary settings, and Appendix D.4 disclosure of full-precision experiments on one NVIDIA A100 80GB GPU.

R1.justification: The references and substantive positioning relative to activation steering, differential privacy, and prior membership-inference attacks are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the abstract by one sentence, makes the threat-model record notation explicit, and adjusts paragraph breaks and a few labels. The section sequence and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 2, 3, and 5 are transposed into narrow tables alongside text; Table 4 becomes full-width, and Table 7 abbreviates its privacy-column headings. These changes reflow surrounding pages, while the figures and appendix displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 makes a small notation clarification and repacks several tables, but preserves the scientific arguments, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations. The more compact layout does not establish a meaningful overall quality gain or loss.
